faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate form of the verb given in brackets to make it a meaningful sentence.
She ___ (hand) me a picture of sloppily drawn birthday cake last year.
faqs.e:
The sentence describes a completed action at a specific past time, marked by 'last year'. This calls for the simple past tense.

Out of the options, only 'Handed' fits as the simple past form of the verb 'hand', making the sentence grammatically correct and meaningful.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate form of the verb given in brackets to make it a meaningful sentence.
I ___ (pull) out my calculator before I added up all the money.
faqs.e:
When two past actions are mentioned and one happened before the other, the earlier action takes the past perfect tense.

Here, pulling out the calculator happened before adding up the money, so 'had pulled' correctly shows this earlier action.

faqs.q: Which of the following sentences is incorrect with reference to reported speech?

options.a: The waiter asked if we wanted a table near the window.
options.b: The teacher asked the students how they wanted to the activity.
options.c: Shamir enquired where was the bus station.
options.d: The guard warned us not to enter the area.

faqs.a: Shamir enquired where was the bus station.
faqs.e:
In reported speech, indirect questions follow normal statement word order (subject before verb), not question word order.

The correct form should be 'Shamir enquired where the bus station was', not 'where was the bus station'.

faqs.q:
Identify the correct passive form of the verb from the options given below.
A nation ___ (hold) together by shared beliefs and shared attitudes.
faqs.e:
The sentence needs a present tense passive form since it describes a general, ongoing truth about nations.

'Is held' correctly matches the singular subject 'A nation' and expresses the passive voice in the present simple tense.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate verb that agrees with the subject in the following sentence.
One of the most important secrets to success ___, instead of being against something, be for something.
faqs.e:
The subject of the sentence is 'One', which is singular, even though it is followed by a plural noun phrase 'secrets to success'.

Since the verb must agree with 'One' and not with 'secrets', the singular verb 'Is' is correct.

faqs.q: Which of the following words has an incorrect spelling?
Identify the grammatically incorrect sentence in passive voice from the options given below.

options.a: These windows in my room really need to be cleaned soon.
options.b: The President is hoping to be elected for a second term.
options.c: Sheela and Swathi might have been invited to the party.
options.d: Raveendra has asked to make a presentation at the meeting by his team leader.

faqs.a: Raveendra has asked to make a presentation at the meeting by his team leader.
faqs.e:
For a sentence to be correctly passive, the verb form must match passive construction throughout.

Here, 'has asked' should be 'has been asked' to correctly show that Raveendra was asked by his team leader, making option (4) grammatically incorrect as written.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with correct preposition in the following sentence.
Great innovators believe that logic and imagination shake hands ___ each other.
faqs.e:
The phrase 'shake hands with' is a fixed prepositional expression used to describe two things coming together or cooperating.

Hence, 'with' is the correct preposition to complete the sentence meaningfully.

faqs.q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'turn the clock back'?

options.a: To restore something to a former condition
options.c: To turn off the alarm clock
options.d: To do things with a jet speed in future

faqs.a: To restore something to a former condition

faqs.q:
Identify the correct form of the following sentence to be converted to direct speech.
'They told us that they would start the admission process the following day.'

options.a: "We will start the admission process tomorrow," they told us.
options.b: We told them, "They will start the admission process tomorrow."
options.c: "We would start the admission process the next day," they told us.
options.d: We told them, "We had to start the admission process tomorrow."

faqs.a: "We will start the admission process tomorrow," they told us.
faqs.e:
When converting reported speech back to direct speech, the tense shifts back to what would have been originally spoken, and 'the following day' becomes 'tomorrow'.

The subject and reporting verb also revert to match who actually spoke, giving option (1) as the correct direct speech version.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate article in the following sentence.
Past glory and education don't count for much. We have to continuously sharpen ___ axe.
faqs.e:
The word 'axe' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article 'an' is used before it.

Since the sentence refers to a general, non-specific axe, 'an' is the appropriate article here.

faqs.q: Identify the correct idiom which means 'accurate information'?

Fill in the blank with correct preposition in the following sentence.
He gaped ___ some developed countries in wonder for their vast materialistic progress.
faqs.e:
The verb 'gape' is typically followed by the preposition 'at' when expressing looking at something with wonder or surprise.

Hence, 'at' correctly completes the sentence.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate article in the following sentence.
People without conviction do not take ___ stand.
faqs.e:
The word 'stand' begins with a consonant sound, so the indefinite article 'a' is used before it.

Since the sentence refers to a general stand and not a specific one, 'a' fits correctly.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate form of the verb given in brackets to make it a meaningful sentence.
Unless you ___ (read) today, you cannot be perfect person tomorrow.
faqs.e:
'Unless' introduces a conditional clause similar to an 'if not' condition, and such clauses typically use the simple present tense to refer to a general or habitual condition.

Hence, 'Read' is the correct form to complete the sentence.

faqs.q:
Fill in the blank with an appropriate pronoun that agrees with the subject in the following sentence.
The biggest achievement of Digital India has been ___ tremendous success in ensuring digital inclusion for all in India.
faqs.e:
The subject 'The biggest achievement' is singular, and the sentence structure requires a verb form that matches this singular subject to describe the ongoing outcome.

'Has' is the form that correctly agrees with the singular subject in this context.

faqs.q:
Identify the correct synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.
'Illustrious people seem to light up everything around them.'

Fill in the blank with correct preposition in the following sentence.
Steve Jobs said, "Innovation distinguishes ___ a leader and a follower."
faqs.e:
The verb 'distinguish' when comparing two things is followed by the preposition 'between'.

Hence, 'between a leader and a follower' is the grammatically correct form.

He was fishing for a squid with pals in shallow water.

Read the passage given below and answer the question.
People wait for the rains since they can ___ in it.
faqs.passage:
The beginning of this fun-filled season with the sun hidden behind the grey clouds brings cheer to many of us waiting eagerly to splash in the rains. Ofcourse not everything about rain is glamorous. Especially when you think about endless traffic jams, the bad roads dotted with potholes, uncleared garbage and the spate of water borne diseases. Also viral infections like cold and cough make their presence felt.

Most infectious diseases prevalent in the rainy season can be prevented by simply washing our hands regularly. Scrubbing hands regularly with water and soap can prevent us from contacting respiratory and diarrheal diseases.

Kids have a lower level of immunity and hence hand washing becomes a crucial part of their lifestyle. When playing especially during monsoon season kids come into contact with germs and can unknowingly become infected simply by touching their nose, eyes or mouth. The Food and Drug Administration states that the human influenza virus can survive on surfaces for up to eight hours, making people susceptible to catching it each time they touch the infected surface. Hence repeated hand washing is required.

To make the best of the rainy season we should follow some simple guidelines. First of all if we decide to get wet in rains we should change into a dry set of clothes at the earliest. Also we should keep raw food items at bay and wash vegetables and fruits thoroughly before use. Moreover, strict kitchen hygiene should be maintained in order to enjoy one of the most beautiful seasons of the year. Also, in order to have a trouble free rainy season home made fresh food should be given preference over the fast food sold in the market.

faqs.q: Let A, B, C, D represent the marks of four students respectively. If the average of A, B, C is 10⅓; B, C, D is 13⅔; C, D, A is 12⅓; and D, A, B is 11⅔; then 5(C-B) =
faqs.e:
The four averages give four equations: A+B+C=31, B+C+D=41, C+D+A=37, D+A+B=35 (each multiplied by 3).

Subtracting the first equation from the second gives D-A, and working through the combinations, subtracting pairs of these equations and simplifying leads to 5(C-B) = D+A-B-C.

faqs.q: Let n be a positive integer and n < 193. If n and 193 are coprime numbers, then the sum of all possible values of n is :
faqs.e:
Since 193 is a prime number, every integer from 1 to 192 is automatically coprime with it (they share no common factors except 1).

So the sum of all possible values of n is simply the sum of the first 192 natural numbers: 192×193/2 = 18528.

faqs.q: A Shopkeeper spent 20% of his profit in a particular month towards wages of his workers. From the remaining profit he spent 10% towards his shop rent and 40% towards his family expenses. He then saved the balance amount of Rs.50,000 in a bank. Then the total amount he spent towards wages and rent is (in Rupees) :
faqs.e:
After spending 20% on wages, 80% of the profit remains. Out of this remaining amount, 50% goes to rent and family expenses combined, leaving the other 50% as savings of ₹50,000.

So the remaining profit is ₹1,00,000, making the total profit ₹1,25,000. Wages = 20% of 1,25,000 = ₹25,000, and rent = 10% of 1,00,000 = ₹10,000. Together, wages and rent total ₹35,000.

faqs.q: If a:b = 3:4, b:c = 4:5, a+2b = 55 and 3b-c = 35 then 3a+2b-c =
faqs.e:
Since a:b = 3:4 and b:c = 4:5 share the same value of b, we get a:b:c = 3:4:5. Using a+2b = 55 with a=3k, b=4k gives 11k=55, so k=5.

This gives a=15, b=20, c=25, which satisfies 3b-c=35. So 3a+2b-c = 45+40-25 = 60.

faqs.q: The distance between two stations A and B is 480 km. A car started from A. But its speed is reduced by 20 kmph than it's usual speed due to road traffic and the usual time of reaching the destination B is increased by 2 hours. Then the usual duration of the total journey is (in hours) :
faqs.e:
Let the usual speed be s km/h, so the usual time is 480/s. With speed reduced to (s-20), the new time becomes 480/(s-20), which is 2 hours more than the usual time.

Solving 480/(s-20) - 480/s = 2 gives s = 80 km/h, so the usual travel time is 480/80 = 6 hours.

faqs.q: The day of the week on 5th September 1887 was :
faqs.e:
September 5th is always a 'doomsday' date, meaning it always falls on the same day of the week as other doomsday dates in a given year.

Calculating the doomsday for the year 1887 using the standard anchor-day method gives Monday, so 5th September 1887 was a Monday.

faqs.q: A started a business by investing Rs. 5,25,000. At the end of 5th month from the commencement of the business B joined A by investing Rs. 4,32,000 and at the end of 8th month from start of the business C joined both A and B by investing Rs. 6,30,000. If C's share in the profit at the end of the year is Rs. 50,000 and A's share is Rs. x more than B's share then x =
faqs.e:
The capital-months invested are: A = 5,25,000×12 = 63,00,000; B = 4,32,000×7 = 30,24,000; C = 6,30,000×4 = 25,20,000.

Since C's share of ₹50,000 corresponds to a ratio of 25,20,000, the total profit works out to about ₹2,35,000. A's share is about ₹1,25,000 and B's share is about ₹60,000, so x = A - B ≈ ₹65,000.

faqs.q: A Can do a work in 6 days and B can do the same work in 9 days. A and B along with a third person C can finish that work in 3 days. If the total wages for the work is Rs. 24,000 then the wages of C is (in Rupees) :
faqs.e:
A's rate is 1/6 and B's rate is 1/9 of the work per day. Since A, B and C together finish the work in 3 days, their combined rate is 1/3.

Subtracting A and B's rates from 1/3 gives C's rate as 1/18, meaning C alone would take 18 days. In 3 days, C does 1/6 of the work, so C's wage is 1/6 of ₹24,000 = ₹4,000.

faqs.q: A rectangular track of 5 meters width is made round a circular field such that each of the inner side of the track touches the field at a point. If the area of the field is 61,600 square meters and the cost of forming the track is Rs. 100 per square meter, then the amount (in Rupees) required for forming the track is
faqs.e:
Since the field's area is 61,600 m² and area = πr², solving with π=22/7 gives the field's radius as 140 m. Adding the 5 m track width gives an outer radius of 145 m.

The track's area is π(145²-140²) = π×5×285, which when multiplied by the cost of ₹100 per square meter gives the total cost required to form the track.

Following the order of operations (BODMAS), 'of' is treated as multiplication and is performed along with division and multiplication before addition and subtraction.

Solving the bracket first, then handling multiplication, division and 'of' from left to right, and finally the addition and subtraction, gives 5041.

faqs.q: A, B, C, D are four persons. A sold an antique to B, B sold it to C and C to D. The price of antique rised on the whole by 80% when it is bought by D. A earned 25% profit and B earned 20% profit then the profit earned by C is :
faqs.e:
Taking A's cost price as 100, A sells to B at a 25% profit, making B's cost 125. B sells to C at a 20% profit, making C's cost 150.

Since the overall price rises by 80% by the time D buys it, D's price is 180. C's profit is then (180-150)/150 × 100 = 20%.

faqs.q: The present age of A is thrice the present age of B. 5 years ago, the age of A was square of the age of B at that time. But 10 years hence, the age of A will be twice the age of B at that time. Then the present age of A (in years) is :
faqs.e:
Let B's present age be b, so A's present age is 3b. From the condition 10 years hence, 3b+10 = 2(b+10), which gives b=10.

Checking with the 5-years-ago condition confirms this works, since 3(10)-5=25 equals (10-5)². So A's present age is 3×10 = 30 years.

faqs.q: By selling an article with a discount of 25% on its marked price, a trader gets a profit of 12½%. If the discount is 30% on its marked price then the gain percent on its cost price is :
faqs.e:
Taking the cost price as 100, a 25% discount giving 12.5% profit means the selling price is 112.5, so the marked price works out to 150.

With a 30% discount instead, the new selling price is 70% of 150 = 105, giving a gain of 5% on the cost price of 100.

faqs.q: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 years at 6% per annum is Rs.22,500 and on the same sum for 4 years at R% per annum simple interest is Rs.40,000. Then the simple interest on the same sum for R years at 7% per annum is (in Rupees) :
faqs.e:
Using SI = PRT/100 for the first case, 22,500 = P×6×3/100 gives the principal as ₹1,25,000. Using this principal in the second case, 40,000 = 1,25,000×R×4/100 gives R = 8%.

Now finding the SI for R years (8 years) at 7%: SI = 1,25,000×7×8/100 = ₹70,000.

faqs.q: A cylindrical container of inner radius 7 cm contains 6 solid spherical balls, each of radius 7 cm. If the top most ball touches the upper lid of the container, then the volume of the empty space in the container is (in cu.cm) :
faqs.e:
Since 6 spheres of radius 7 cm are stacked and the cylinder's radius equals the sphere's radius, the cylinder's height equals 6 times the sphere's diameter, i.e., 6×14 = 84 cm.

The cylinder's volume is π×7²×84 = 12936 cm³, and the total volume of the 6 spheres is 6×(4/3)×π×7³ = 8624 cm³. The empty space is 12936 - 8624 = 4312 cm³.

faqs.q: It is given that, if two pipes of radii r₁ and r₂ can fill an empty tank in t₁ minutes and t₂ minutes respectively and the speed of the flow is same in both the pipes then t₁r₁² = t₂r₂². There are three taps of diameters 1 cm, 1½ cm, and 2 cm respectively. The speed of the water flow through them is same. The widest tap can fill an empty tank in 45 minutes. If all the taps are opened simultaneously, then in how many hours will the empty tank be filled?
faqs.e:
Since t×d² is constant for all taps, and the widest tap (diameter 2) takes 45 minutes, the constant value is 45×4=180. This gives the fill times for the other taps as 180 minutes and 80 minutes.

Adding up all three individual rates (1/180+1/80+1/45) and taking the reciprocal gives the combined time as 720/29 minutes, which equals 12/29 hours.

faqs.q: If the HCF of 546, 1155, 462 and 1365 is H and LCM of 252, 504, 108 is L then L/H =
faqs.e:
Breaking each number into prime factors, the common factors across 546, 1155, 462 and 1365 are 3 and 7, so their HCF is H = 21.

For the LCM of 252, 504 and 108, taking the highest powers of all prime factors present gives L = 1512. So L/H = 1512/21 = 72.

faqs.q: A train can cross a platform in 18 sec with its usual speed. It can cross the same platform in 15 sec if its usual speed is increased by 15 kmph. If the length of the platform is 1½ times that of the train, then the usual speed (in kmph) of the train is :
faqs.e:
Let the train's length be L, so the platform is 1.5L, and the total distance to cross is 2.5L. Setting up the equations for both speeds (in consistent units) and equating the distance covered in each case.

Solving the two equations together gives the usual speed of the train as 75 km/h.

For x, solving x² = 3080+x gives x = 56. For y, solving y² = 200y gives y = 200. So z = x+y = 256.

The nested expression √(z√(z√z)) simplifies to z raised to the power 7/8. Since z = 256 = 2⁸, this equals 2⁷ = 128.

faqs.q: A watch loses 5 min in every 24 hours duration and another watch gains 3 min in the same duration. If both the watches show identical time 't' at a particular point of time, then by what time duration (in days) will they both show the same identical time 't' again in near future?
faqs.e:
Since one watch loses 5 minutes and the other gains 3 minutes every 24 hours, the two watches drift apart from each other by 8 minutes every day.

For both watches to show the same time again on a 12-hour dial, the total drift must reach 720 minutes (12 hours). Dividing 720 by the daily drift of 8 minutes gives 90 days.

faqs.q: The divisor of 7280 among the following is :
faqs.e:
Breaking 7280 into its prime factors gives 7280 = 2⁴×5×7×13.

Checking each option against these factors, only 182 = 2×7×13 divides 7280 exactly (7280÷182 = 40), making it the correct divisor.

faqs.q: A sum of money invested at interest, compounded annually, amounts to Rs. 7680 in 2 years and Rs. 8192 in 3 years. Then the sum of money (in Rs.) invested is :
faqs.e:
The ratio of the amount after 3 years to after 2 years gives (1+r) = 8192/7680 = 16/15.

Using P(1+r)² = 7680 with (1+r)² = 256/225, the principal P = 7680×225/256 = ₹6,750.

faqs.q: 8 men can do a piece of work in 12 days, 9 women can do the same work in 16 days and 12 children can do it in 24 days. 6 men, 12 women and 18 children started that work and worked together for 3 days. If only women have to complete the remaining work on the 4th day, the number of women required is :
faqs.e:
One man's daily work rate is 1/96, one woman's is 1/144, and one child's is 1/288 of the total work. In 3 days, 6 men, 12 women and 18 children together complete about 0.625 of the work, leaving 0.375 remaining.

Since each woman does 1/144 of the work per day, the number of women needed to finish 0.375 of the work in one day is 0.375×144 = 54.

faqs.q: If x, y, z are any three non-zero real numbers such that x⁴-y²=z², y⁴-z²=x² and z⁴-x²=y² then (x²+1)⁻¹+(y²+1)⁻¹+(z²+1)⁻¹ =
faqs.e:
Adding all three given equations shows that x⁴+y⁴+z⁴-(x²+y²+z²) equals x²+y²+z², which leads to a relationship connecting x², y² and z².

Using this relationship and simplifying the sum of the three reciprocal terms algebraically shows that the expression always equals 1.

faqs.q: 0.7̄ is multiplied by itself and that result is divided by (2/9)ᵗʰ part of the reciprocal of 0.8̄. If the value thus obtained is x, then 9√x =
faqs.e:
0.7̄ equals 7/9, so squaring it gives 49/81. The reciprocal of 0.8̄ (which is 8/9) is 9/8, and (2/9)th of this is 1/4.

Dividing 49/81 by 1/4 gives x = 196/81. Taking 9√x = 9×(14/9) = 14.
